Clearly the 'Industry' has steadied and mastered their process for licensing and pushing out anime. But what about manga? As a very different medium with a higher quantity of content coming out at different intervals, manga cannot be treated as anime is while maintaining the same level of coverage and quality.

  • How's the manga coverage where you live?
  • What do you think is being done correctly?
  • What do you think could be improved?
  • Overall, what do you think is the optimal way legal manga would work?
[Discussion] Legal Manga - What's working? What could be better?

In Houston there are plenty of places to buy Manga. Barnes & Noble, comicbook shops, Half-Priced books and the like. I think it's done well here. There's a vast selection, but I don't read the translated manga, because I like to keep my Japanese up and it loses something in translation. I think ebooks from online stores and subscription services are the best legal ways to get manga.

How's the manga coverage where you live?

I live near Austin and San Antonio, so there are a lot of niche shops I can go to to access manga, but outside of those secluded areas it's as obscure as ever. Honestly, sitting here thinking about it, it's not too bad. I can pick up any mainstream listing I want, or special order pretty much anything that's still in print. Crunchyroll and Viz both mitigate the scarcity of (some) current releases, too.

What do you think is being done correctly?

It looks like more and more series are being licensed for official US release. Also, even though it's niche, anime and manga are going from being buried in the dark corners of a comicbook shop to holding prime shelving in traditional stores like B&N.

What do you think could be improved?

As @amar771 said English releases (outside of the simulpubs by Crunchyroll/Viz) are slow, and worst of all limited. You can go through Bleach, One Piece, Naruto, and Case Closed until your eyes bleed, but good like finding Angel Densetsu, Baby Steps, Haikyu!!, and Black Bullet (though admittedly v1 of BB is coming out this month, and v2 is coming out in December).

Overall, what do you think is the optimal way legal manga would work?

Speedy releases of everything. If it's available in Japan, make it available here. If the big publishers won't do it, then smaller ones need to.

How's the manga coverage where you live?

Live in South Florida and there are two local comic book shops that have some manga. Mostly Naruto, one piece, fairy tail, etc. Besides that I have to go to Barnes and nobles for more manga or Amazon for everything else. Even then their sections are crappy.

What do you think is being done correctly?

It being available to buy online, like amazon and ebay.

What do you think could be improved?

A Spotify of manga. You pay a monthly fee, get access to a bunch of manga and can search by genres and have an accurate list.

Overall, what do you think is the optimal way legal manga would work?

Like stated above, a Spotify of manga and you can choose to purchase volumes of a manga, depending on the size of an order or how many times a customer buys a month, can lead to discounts and promos. But since buying physical copies can get pretty expensive, I would look for a way to make that cheaper. I would also like more access to raw manga. It would also be cool if shonen jump did a monthly English version here every week.
